copilot-app-builder.title: FAQ: App Builder in Microsoft 365 Copilot – Microsoft Learn
copilot-app-builder.notes: App Builder is an agent inside Microsoft Copilot that lets people describe an app in everyday language and have it generated, saved and shared. The resulting apps are meant for interactive prototypes, data visualization and productivity tools for the author or their team. The AI produces code from the description and builds app pages in real time during a conversational exchange, and users can keep refining elements, layout and behavior afterwards. Context such as images, people, tags, meetings and Word, PowerPoint or Excel documents can be supplied as input, and users can rate results with thumbs up or down and comments. Documented limits: complex design requirements are difficult, data connections are restricted to Microsoft Lists with create, read, update and delete operations, the generated code cannot be edited by hand, and only English is supported. The page advises describing simple problems clearly and testing apps thoroughly before sharing them. It also notes that app building is now offered in Copilot Cowork and is planned for Microsoft Copilot Studio.

copilot-flex-routing.title: Copilot flex routing – Microsoft Learn
copilot-flex-routing.notes: Flex routing is a setting for customers in the EU and EFTA that lets large language model inferencing take place outside the EU Data Boundary during periods of high demand, so Copilot stays consistent under load. It applies to Microsoft Copilot and Copilot Chat in the Microsoft 365 admin center, and to Copilot experiences in Dynamics 365, Power Platform and Copilot Studio in the Power Platform admin center. When active, processing may occur in the United States, Canada or Australia, while data stays encrypted in transit and at rest, and stored data remains inside the EU Data Boundary apart from limited pseudonymized data kept for security and operations. An administrator with the AI Administrator role chooses between allowing flex routing during peak load or not allowing it, and can change the choice at any time. The Power Platform setting inherits the Microsoft 365 choice unless it is stricter. Tenants using Multi-Geo are out of scope for the Microsoft 365 setting. For eligible tenants created after late March 2026 it is on by default, and older tenants are asked to review it.

copilot-researcher-agent.title: Researcher agent in Microsoft 365 Copilot – Microsoft Learn
copilot-researcher-agent.notes: Researcher is an assistant within Microsoft Copilot built for complex, multi-step research tasks and produces well-sourced, comprehensive reports. It draws on web information as well as work content the user can already access, such as files, emails, meetings and chats, and it respects the same permissions, policies and compliance rules as the rest of the work environment. Output can include structured sections, charts and other visualizations, and citations. The agent may ask clarifying questions so the person can steer the work, and the search scope can be set to work resources, the web, or both. It is reached by signing in to the Microsoft Copilot app and choosing it under Agents in chat. Typical uses are analyses combining several sources and reports meant for sharing or decisions. Because processing takes longer, it is less suitable for quick tasks such as summarizing a short email, where standard Copilot Chat is recommended. Result quality depends on precise prompts and a clearly defined search scope.

copilot-studio-topics.title: Create and edit topics – Microsoft Copilot Studio
copilot-studio-topics.notes: A topic in Copilot Studio defines one part of the conversation between a user and an agent. It is built on an authoring canvas from one or more nodes, each performing an action such as sending a message or asking a question, which together set the possible conversation paths. This gives a no-code way for an agent to answer questions, take actions and resolve problems. System topics cover basics like escalating to a person or ending a conversation; they cannot be created or deleted but can be turned off and edited. Custom topics include predefined ones such as greeting and any the maker creates. Node types include message, question, adaptive card, condition, variable management, topic management, tools and advanced nodes for generative answers or HTTP requests. Trigger phrases should be short, and with classic orchestration the agent matches topics by phrases and language understanding, while generative orchestration chooses topics from their descriptions. A code editor with YAML is available, though designing complex topics fully in code is not fully supported. Topic names should avoid periods, because such an agent cannot be exported as a solution.

credit-and-collections.title: Credit and collections overview – Dynamics 365 Finance – Microsoft Learn
credit-and-collections.notes: This overview covers two related areas of accounts receivable in Dynamics 365 Finance. Credit management controls customer credit limits and uses rule-based credit rules to decide how sales orders move through posting. Collections management handles receivables and the collection activities needed when payments are overdue. On the credit side, users maintain credit attributes for assessing customers, create limits including temporary adjustments, record insurance and guarantees, and group customers so they share one limit. Risk scores can be assigned and used to generate limits automatically. Blocking rules place orders on hold based on factors such as risk, payment terms, limit, overdue amounts and limit utilization, and a workflow can approve limit changes and order releases. On the collections side, a central Collections page offers customer lists built from predefined criteria and customer pools, including pools per collector, with all collection information for a customer on one page. Interest and fees can be waived, reinstated or reversed, write-offs created and non-sufficient-funds payments processed in a single step, and customer aging snapshots capture aging as of a date. The page is a conceptual overview and points to separate setup articles.

custom-pages.title: Custom pages overview for model-driven apps – Power Apps – Microsoft Learn
custom-pages.notes: A custom page is a page type for model-driven apps that brings canvas app capabilities into them. It can appear as a full page, a dialog or a side panel, and it is authored in Power Apps Studio with low-code formulas and custom Power Apps component framework controls. Compared with forms, views and dashboards it is more flexible: it can bind to one or more tables, works with Dataverse and the Power Apps connectors, and supports responsive layouts through responsive container controls. Navigation uses the Power Fx navigate function, and model-driven pages open a custom page through the navigateTo client API; pages can also be added to the site map. It must be created from within a solution, is a single solution component that only one maker can edit at a time, and follows the licensing and sharing of the model-driven app. A model-driven app can contain up to 25 custom pages. Standalone canvas apps are not supported as custom pages, and embedded canvas apps remain limited to forms. The page positions custom pages as the usual replacement for embedded canvas apps.

customer-intent-agent.title: Set up the Customer Intent Agent – Dynamics 365 Contact Center – Microsoft Learn
customer-intent-agent.notes: The Customer Intent Agent discovers customer intents from historical data and maintains a current intent library whose entries carry attributes for intent detection, interviewing and fulfillment. The stated aim is higher deflection rates, and intent plus interview answers also improve generated responses for Copilot agents and human service representatives. On escalation, the intent and the interview questions already asked are passed along so the representative can address open items. Each intent is switched on through a checkbox labelled Use in AI Agents, and a component collection called intent-based suggestions is added in Microsoft Copilot Studio. Redirect variables control hand-offs for resolved issues, unknown intent, inability to proceed, customer-requested escalation and errors, while an enrichment context variable carries data collected earlier, for example from a pre-chat survey. Requirements include enabled intent discovery, a Copilot agent linked to a knowledge source and an omnichannel workstream, the Environment Maker role, and a Dataverse connection reference set up by an administrator. Component updates only arrive after the agent is republished manually.

d365-custom-services.title: Custom services – Dynamics 365 Finance and Operations – Microsoft Learn
d365-custom-services.notes: Custom services are services that developers create for Finance and Operations apps so that X++ classes can be consumed from outside. A custom service is written under a service group, and a service group is always deployed on two endpoints: a SOAP endpoint and a JSON endpoint. The SOAP variant matches the behavior known from Dynamics AX 2012: every service group under the AOT service group node is deployed automatically, and any service that should be exposed must belong to a service group. In a non-development environment the SOAP address follows the pattern of the base URL, a soap and services path, the service name and a wsdl query. The JSON variant returns its data set in JSON and is addressed with a path made of the host, an api and services segment, the service group name, the service name within that group and the operation name. Sample code for both styles, a SOAP console application and a JSON console application, is kept in the Microsoft Dynamics AX Integration repository on GitHub. The page does not describe licensing, authentication or throughput limits, and names no specific integration scenarios.

dataverse-alternate-keys.title: Use an alternate key to reference a record – Dataverse – Microsoft Learn
dataverse-alternate-keys.notes: Alternate keys let integration scenarios work with a Dataverse row when its primary key value is not known. They apply only to tables for which they have been defined, and most tables have none unless customized. They can be defined in Power Apps or in code and are used through the Dataverse Web API or the SDK for .NET, although this page walks through the Web API only. A row is referenced by a URL, for example with an account number in parentheses, with several key columns separated by commas for a multi-part key, or with a lookup-based column. These URLs work with POST, PATCH and DELETE and can also set single-valued navigation properties with the odata.bind annotation. Using a column that is not defined as a unique key causes an error. The characters slash, angle brackets, asterisk, percent, ampersand, colon, backslash, question mark and plus are not supported in key values, and parameter aliases do not work in this syntax. A workaround is to query the collection with a filter and reuse the returned ID. The system user and team types inherit from principal, whose primary key is the owner ID.

dataverse-custom-api.title: Create and use Custom APIs – Dataverse – Microsoft Learn
dataverse-custom-api.notes: A Dataverse custom API is a code-first way to define custom messages, bundling one or more operations into an API that developers can call from code or from Power Automate. It is presented as an alternative to custom process actions, which are no-code but give developers fewer options. Its parts are request parameters, response properties and an optional plug-in holding the main logic. A binding type of global, entity or entity collection decides the scope, and the Is Function setting makes it either a function called with GET that only returns data or an action called with POST and parameters in the body. The allowed custom processing step type controls whether other steps may react asynchronously or also change and cancel the behavior. Further options include marking the API private, requiring an execute privilege, enabling it in the workflow designer and basing business events on it. It can be created with the Plug-in Registration Tool, the Power Apps maker portal, Web API code or solution files. Known limits include a size cap on function URLs, rejected special characters in function string literals, no change of function or action afterwards, and no configuration data for the main-logic plug-in.

dataverse-virtual-tables.title: Create and edit virtual tables – Dataverse – Microsoft Learn
dataverse-virtual-tables.notes: A virtual table is a custom Dataverse table whose columns hold data from an external source such as an Azure SQL database. To users its rows look like ordinary records and appear in all clients, yet the connection is made at runtime without replicating the data. Earlier approaches needed a connector to move the data or a custom plug-in. The pieces are a data provider, made of plug-ins and a data source table, a data source row describing the connection parameters, and the virtual table that points to that source. Dataverse ships connector-based providers for sources such as SQL Server, SharePoint and Fabric, plus an OData v4 provider, and developers can build their own providers. Makers create the table from a solution in Power Apps and set up the data source under the advanced settings, where a data source secret can hold sensitive values. Limits are considerable: existing tables cannot be converted, system columns and some data types are unsupported, and there is no auditing, change tracking, offline mode, business process flows or row-level Dataverse security. Dashboards and charts are not supported, and the data is not synchronized through Azure Synapse Link.

dax-addcolumns-function.title: ADDCOLUMNS function (DAX) – Microsoft Learn
dax-addcolumns-function.notes: ADDCOLUMNS is a DAX function that adds calculated columns to a table or table expression. Its syntax takes a table, followed by one or more pairs of a column name in double quotes and an expression. The table argument can be any DAX expression that returns a table, and each expression must return a scalar value, which is evaluated for every row of that table. The result is a table that keeps all original columns and includes the added ones. The page lists it as applicable in calculated columns, calculated tables, measures and visual calculations. Its worked example extends a product category table with internet sales and reseller sales, each computed by summing a related sales table row by row; a category without matching internet sales, such as components, shows a blank in that column. The one documented restriction is that ADDCOLUMNS is not supported in DirectQuery mode when used in calculated columns or in row-level security rules. The page gives no performance guidance and no licensing requirements.

dax-time-intelligence.title: Time intelligence functions (DAX) – Microsoft Learn
dax-time-intelligence.notes: DAX offers a family of time intelligence functions for working with data over periods such as days, months, quarters and years, so that calculations over those periods can be built and compared. Before any of them is used, one of the tables containing a date column has to be marked as a date table. The functions fall into several groups. Start and end functions return the first or last date of a week, month, quarter or year, including first date and last date. Opening and closing balance functions evaluate an expression at the beginning or end of a period. To-date functions such as the year, quarter, month and week variants return either cumulative values or date tables up to the current date. Shifting and comparison functions include DATEADD, PARALLELPERIOD and SAMEPERIODLASTYEAR, ranges can be set with DATESBETWEEN and DATESINPERIOD, and previous and next day, week, month, quarter and year functions step to neighboring periods. The documentation applies to Power BI, Analysis Services and the DAX language in general. Beyond the date table requirement it states no restrictions and refers to the individual function pages for detail.

declarative-agent.title: Declarative agents overview – Microsoft 365 Copilot extensibility – Microsoft Learn
declarative-agent.notes: A declarative agent gives a focused conversational experience powered by Microsoft 365 Copilot, where the builder defines the purpose, instructions, knowledge sources and supported actions for a business scenario. It suits cases where users need a dedicated dialogue with behavior and capabilities tailored to one outcome. The definition covers identity and behavior, such as name, instructions, conversation starters, constraints and appearance, plus grounding knowledge, capabilities such as actions, skills, connectors or tools including MCP-based ones, and host and distribution metadata so it appears in supported Microsoft surfaces. Typical examples are employee support answering common questions from approved company knowledge and customer support combining instructions, knowledge and an external capability like looking up order information. An agent is unnecessary when the needed capability is already available in a supported surface or an existing shared agent fits. When full control over orchestration, model, hosting or interface is required, the page points to custom engine agents. Teams are advised to document audience, permissions, data boundaries, licensing and owners. Government cloud support differs, with GCC fully supported and DoD limited to pro-code agents.

default-azure-credential.title: DefaultAzureCredential class – azure-identity – Microsoft Learn
default-azure-credential.notes: DefaultAzureCredential, in the Python azure.identity package, is a credential intended to cover most authentication scenarios of the Azure SDK. The identity actually used depends on the environment. When an access token is needed, the class tries a fixed sequence of sources and stops at the first one that returns a token. The sequence starts with a service principal configured through environment variables, then workload identity, then a managed identity, then on Windows a user signed in through a Microsoft application via the shared token cache. After that come the identity signed in to Visual Studio Code, the Azure CLI, Azure PowerShell and the Azure Developer CLI, and finally brokered authentication on Windows and WSL when the azure-identity-broker package is installed. Keyword arguments can exclude individual sources, require an environment variable naming the allowed credentials, set a subprocess timeout, pick a user-assigned managed identity by client ID, or change the authority. The interactive browser source is excluded by default. Methods include get_token, get_token_info and close. If every source fails, a ClientAuthenticationError lists each attempt, and at least one scope must be passed.

default-environment.title: Manage the default environment – Power Platform – Microsoft Learn
default-environment.notes: The default environment in Power Platform is available to every employee of an organization that uses the platform and is designed for personal productivity, so all users are potential makers. Apps and flows live there, and custom SharePoint forms create canvas apps in it unless another environment is chosen. Data policies control which connectors may be used, though some core connectors, such as Exchange, cannot be blocked. Admins can turn on managed environment features like sharing limits, usage insights, an IP firewall for Dataverse and the actions page with recommendations, and can quarantine canvas apps with PowerShell cmdlets. Backups are automatic and a restore can go into a developer environment. The page flags risks: orphaned resources appear when makers leave, apps lack proper lifecycle management, and flows started from SharePoint always use this environment. Valuable apps should be moved to their own managed environments, and the CoE Starter Kit is an optional monitoring aid. Restoring the default environment can also bring back orphaned apps and flows that had been cleaned up.

deployment-slots.title: Set up staging environments in Azure App Service – Microsoft Learn
deployment-slots.notes: A deployment slot in Azure App Service is a separate live app with its own host name that can be used for deployments instead of the default production slot. Content and configuration can be swapped between two slots, including with production. This allows changes to be validated before they go live, and all instances of the slot are warmed up first, so the page states there is no downtime and requests are not dropped during a swap. After a swap the source slot holds the previous production version, which can be restored by swapping again. Features include standard swap, swap with preview that can be completed or cancelled, auto swap after a code push, and traffic routing that sends a chosen percentage of requests to a slot. Some settings travel with the swap, such as app settings not marked as slot settings, while custom domains, scale settings and managed identities stay with the slot. Several slots require the Standard, Premium or Isolated tiers, and slots add no extra cost. Auto swap is unavailable for Linux web apps, and swap with preview does not work when site authentication is enabled in one of the slots.

desktop-flow.title: Introduction to desktop flows – Power Automate – Microsoft Learn
desktop-flow.notes: Desktop flows extend the robotic process automation capabilities of Power Automate and are meant to automate repetitive tasks on the desktop. They are built and run through the Power Automate application for Windows, where a designer offers prebuilt drag-and-drop actions and users can also record their own flows for later playback. Available actions cover files and folders as well as web and Excel automation, and a flow can control applications through UI elements, images or screen coordinates. This lets it automate legacy applications such as terminal emulators, modern web and desktop applications, Excel files and folders. Examples named on the page include organizing documents into files and folders, extracting data from websites into Excel, and entering data into ERP systems. Signing in can be done with a Microsoft account, a work or school account, or an organization premium account, and the feature differences by account type are described in the setup article. The page itself gives no pricing, system requirements or limits and points to known issues and limitations elsewhere.

device-code-flow.title: OAuth 2.0 device authorization grant flow – Microsoft identity platform – Microsoft Learn
device-code-flow.notes: The Microsoft identity platform supports the OAuth 2.0 device authorization grant, which lets people sign in on input-constrained devices such as smart TVs, IoT devices or printers. The device shows a code, the user signs in on another device that has a browser, and the original device then receives access and refresh tokens. The client first posts its application ID and requested scopes to the device code endpoint of the tenant and receives a device code, a user code, a verification address, a lifetime and a polling interval. After showing the user code and address, the client polls the token endpoint using the device code grant type, handling responses such as authorization pending, declined, bad verification code and expired token. A successful reply contains a bearer access token, plus an ID token with the openid scope and a refresh token with the offline access scope. An app registration in Microsoft Entra is required. The code expires after a limited time, the complete verification address option is not supported, and personal accounts require the user to sign in again in the browser. Microsoft recommends the MSAL libraries where possible.

device-compliance.title: Device compliance policies overview – Microsoft Intune – Microsoft Learn
device-compliance.notes: Intune compliance policies are sets of rules and conditions used to evaluate the configuration of managed devices, and a device counts as compliant only when it meets all configured conditions. The aim is to protect organizational data from devices that do not meet requirements, and results feed Microsoft Entra Conditional Access, which can grant or block access depending on compliance state. There are tenant-wide compliance policy settings, such as how devices with no assigned policy are marked and how long a compliance status stays valid, plus platform-specific policies assigned to users or device groups. Each platform needs its own policy, covering Android variants, iOS and iPadOS, Linux, macOS and Windows. Rules can require a minimum or maximum operating system version, no jailbreak or root, or a threat level from threat-defense software. Non-compliance actions include marking the device, emailing users, remote lock and marking it for retirement, and custom compliance settings allow additional checks on some platforms. Devices with no policy are compliant by default, so the page suggests changing that when Conditional Access is used, and evaluation depends on the device check-in cycle.

digital-twin-builder.title: Digital twin builder (preview) overview – Microsoft Fabric – Microsoft Learn
digital-twin-builder.notes: Digital twin builder is a preview item in the Real-Time Intelligence workload of Microsoft Fabric that creates digital representations of real environments so physical operations can be optimized with data. Users model business concepts such as assets and processes through an ontology, map data from different source systems onto it, and define semantic relationships across a system or site. The page describes a low-code and no-code approach aimed at operational decision makers. Main parts are ontology modeling with entity types, ontology mapping of source data to entity instances, contextualization through relationship types, and an explorer with a map of assets, time series charts, keyword search and advanced queries. Extensions include public APIs, deployment pipelines, a Fabric data agent for questions about twin data, machine learning, Power BI, real-time dashboards and Activator for alerts. Data is stored in OneLake and available to other Fabric workloads, but it must first be brought into a Fabric lakehouse before loading. The page states explicitly that this item is not the same as the Azure Digital Twins service, and it does not discuss licensing or capacity.

digital-twins-definition-language.title: Understand twin models in Azure Digital Twins (DTDL) – Microsoft Learn
digital-twins-definition-language.notes: The Digital Twins Definition Language is the language Azure Digital Twins uses to describe models. It is based on JSON-LD, independent of any programming language, and is also used by IoT Plug and Play. A model resembles a class in object-oriented languages and defines the data shape of a concept such as a room or a temperature sensor, and digital twins are later created as instances of these models. An interface has an identifier in the DTMI format, a type, a context, an optional display name and a contents array holding properties, relationships and components. Properties carry state data with primitive, object, map, enum and semantic types, relationships link twins, components compose other interfaces without separate identity in the graph, and interfaces can extend one or more parents. Versions 2 and 3 are supported, with version 3 recommended and some limits when mixing them. Commands are not supported, the writable and multiplicity attributes are not enforced, interfaces cannot be defined inline, and components can nest only one level. The Azure Digital Twins Explorer fully supports version 2 but only partly version 3. Uploading models requires an Azure Digital Twins instance.

distribution-list.title: Manage distribution groups in Exchange Online – Microsoft Learn
distribution-list.notes: A distribution list in Exchange Online is a group type used only for distributing email to a fixed set of recipients. Its membership is maintained statically, unlike dynamic distribution groups whose members are calculated from rules. The page names four message-capable group types, distribution lists, dynamic distribution groups, mail-enabled security groups and Microsoft 365 groups, and covers only the first. Lists are created, changed and removed in the Exchange admin center or Exchange Online PowerShell, and PowerShell exposes some properties and bulk changes the admin center lacks. Settings include name, description and addresses, owners and members with at least one owner required, hiding the list from the global address list, delivery management for internal or external senders, Send As and Send on Behalf delegation, moderation, and open, closed or owner-approved join and leave rules. Supported members include mailboxes, mail users, mail contacts and mail-enabled groups, while Microsoft 365 groups and Entra users without mail are not supported. Filtering in the admin center can be inconsistent for very large groups, and for collaboration with files and chat a Microsoft 365 group is the intended choice.

dlp-simulation-mode.title: Learn about data loss prevention simulation mode – Microsoft Purview – Microsoft Learn
dlp-simulation-mode.notes: Simulation mode for data loss prevention policies replaces the earlier test and test with policy tips states. The policy runs as if it were enforced, but nothing is actually enforced, and the results are kept separate from those of enforced policies in an isolated environment. The purpose is to see a policy's impact before enforcement, tune it and reduce false positives without disturbing users or business processes. Three tabs present the outcome: an overview showing status, scan status per location, items scanned and total matches, a list of items for review with source item and metadata, and a list of alerts in the style of the DLP alerts console. A common pattern is to copy a production policy, change the copy, run it in simulation and, if the result is good, switch the original off and enforce the copy. Simulations can run for a limited time and are not a snapshot. For SharePoint and OneDrive, existing and new items are evaluated, while for Exchange, Teams and devices only items created during the simulation are assessed. Simulation alerts show only in the simulation view and not in the DLP alerts console or the Defender portal. The page lists no licensing information.

dynamic-distribution-group.title: Create and manage dynamic distribution groups – Exchange Online – Microsoft Learn
dynamic-distribution-group.notes: A dynamic distribution group is a mail-enabled group object that speeds up bulk mailing inside an Exchange organization. It has no fixed member list; membership is derived from defined rules. There are two kinds of rules: pre-canned filters, available in the admin center and PowerShell, which use attributes such as state or province, company, department and the custom attributes and can only be combined with AND, and custom recipient filters, available only in PowerShell, which allow other attributes and operators. Eligible recipients include users with mailboxes, mail users and contacts with external addresses, resource mailboxes and mail-enabled groups. Membership is calculated on creation, when rules change and by a refresh at least daily, so attribute changes can take time to apply, and a recipient whose attributes happen to match may receive messages. Pre-canned values must match exactly, prefix wildcards are not supported in custom filters, and custom-filter groups cannot be edited in the admin center. A preview of members is available only in PowerShell. These groups are not synchronized to Microsoft Entra ID or on-premises Active Directory, so Conditional Access cannot be scoped to one. Typical uses are groups by department or custom attribute.
